title: Two triangles, perspective from point and line
body: Desargues' theorem says if lines through corresponding vertices of two triangles meet in one point, then intersections of corresponding sides lie on one line, and conversely. It is self-dual, swapping points and lines throughout. The result organizes projective geometry the way a keystone organises an arch, and its 3D proof is easier than its 2D one, a known scandal of elegance.
